# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Establish this code with Deaf: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3, 🖐 means wire 4, and ✋ means wire 5. Then tell me the manual's exact rule, and relay Deaf's display, light, colour, marking, and wire observations to me precisely.

I will establish the requested wire-number gesture code for Deaf, then encode the manual’s five rows in the manual’s displayed color order: blue, green, red, white, yellow. The corresponding cut-wire numbers are 2, 4, 3, 1, and 5. Deaf can then verbalize this rule and relay the bomb observations to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐", "🤟", "☝", "✋"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Ignore earlier gestures. I am defining this code: the next gesture means white.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]
Deaf says to Mute: The next gesture means red.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌]
Deaf says to Mute: The next gesture means yellow.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟]
Deaf says to Mute: The next gesture means blue.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐]
Deaf says to Mute: The next gesture means green.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋]
Deaf says to Mute: The display is white.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]
Deaf says to Mute: The five gestures that follow are wire colors 1 through 5, in order.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋]
Blind says to Mute: Report now: the manual rule, all observations Deaf has sent, and whether the wire-number code was successfully conveyed. Do not summarize; preserve exact order and markings.

Deaf’s new code supersedes the earlier wire-number code, so the original code was not successfully conveyed. I will signal that failure, then transmit the manual’s exact five light-to-cut-wire-color pairs using Deaf’s newly defined color code. Deaf already has the display and wire-color observations in their exact order and can relay them to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖", "🤟", "✋", "☝", "✌", "✌", "☝", "✋", "🤟", "🖖"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot safely interpret the extra gestures. Please resend only the required wire numbers, using this code: white means wire 1, red means wire 2, yellow means wire 3, blue means wire 4, green means wire 5. Use 🖖 only as start and end markers, and use 👎 if no wire should be acted on.
Blind says to Mute: I received no report. Please speak the manual rule and every Deaf observation to me in your next turn. Ask Deaf for the exact display, light, and all five wire markings, then translate them into words; do not use gestures as the relay to me.

The manual rule is: cut the wire whose color is listed beside the observed light. The display is white, and Deaf’s five wire markings, in wire order, are white, red, yellow, blue, green. Therefore the required color is green, which is wire 5 under Deaf’s current code. I cannot speak to Blind; I will send Deaf the safely delimited instruction for wire 5 and rely on Deaf’s next spoken turn to relay the observations.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖", "✋", "🖖"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I read your latest signal as wire 5. Please state the exact manual action for display 0 and white light to Blind in your next turn.
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

For a white light, the manual requires cutting the green wire. Under Deaf’s current code, green means wire 5, which was correctly cut. I cannot speak to Blind, so I will signal Deaf the required color again; Deaf can state the action aloud.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: New bomb state after the correct cut: display 0, light yellow; wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue, wire 4 white, wire 5 is CUT. Please use the manual and tell Blind the exact next action.
Blind says to Mute: The first cut was correct. Current state: display 0, light yellow; remaining wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white. What exact manual instruction gives the next wire?

The yellow light requires cutting the blue wire. Deaf’s current color code maps blue to wire 4, so the next action is wire 4—not wire 3. I will send the delimited wire-4 instruction to Deaf, who can state the exact manual action to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖", "🖖", "🖖", "🖖", "🖖"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Please speak the exact manual instruction to Blind now. Current state remains display 0, yellow light; wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue, wire 4 white, wire 5 cut. Do not use delimiter gestures alone.
Blind says to Mute: Please send the exact manual instruction for the current state now: display 0, yellow light, remaining wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white. I need the specific next wire.

I cannot speak to Blind directly. The exact manual instruction is to cut the blue wire; from the stated remaining wires, that is wire 3, not wire 4. Deaf’s color-to-wire code says blue means wire 4, but that conflicts with Deaf’s own current wire observations, where wire 3 is blue and wire 4 is white. I will relay the manual’s exact color instruction to Deaf using the established color code, with delimiters.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖", "🖐", "🖖"])
```
